clue.text: Oriental master at sea in this vessel?

definitions.note: the clue as a whole describes the ship it names

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East, so Oriental gives E

explanation.surface: A master mariner from the East is sailing aboard some ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns E (Oriental) plus MASTER into a new arrangement; the question mark flags that 'this vessel' is defined by the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-driven ship is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Unfrock clergy in penitential garb

parts.note: to unfrock a priest is to dismiss him, i.e. sack him
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A defrocked priest is made to wear clothes of repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sacking was worn in mourning or penance, as in the phrase 'in sackcloth and ashes'.

clue.text: Feeling it's a turn-up for the first book

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: the first is No. 1, written NO plus I for one
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at an unexpected development in the opening book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a turn-up for the book' is an idiom for a surprise; here 'turn-up' reverses NO I TOME (No. 1 tome, the first book).
explanation.definitionFit: Emotion is a synonym of feeling, as in a strong sentiment.

clue.text: Curious names, eg an element

indicators.note: curious suggests odd or peculiar, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some odd names given, for example, to a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a metallic chemical element, number 25.

clue.text: Sway to sweet music

definitions.meaning: to sway is to move gently to and fro
a hard stick of seaside candy sold in Britain
a genre of loud popular music

explanation.definitionFit: Rock means to move to and fro, a British stick of candy, and a style of popular music.

clue.text: A prize for wasting away

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone is awarded a prize for withering away.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the medical term for a body part shrinking from disuse.

clue.text: A north Greek region takes it in for fuel

indicators.note: takes and in together tell us one piece is taken inside another
in, with takes, places the small word inside the region

parts.note: Thrace is a historical region of northern Greece
taken as written

explanation.surface: A region in northern Greece stockpiles something to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is split: 'takes' and 'in' together, with 'it' between them, signal the insertion into the ancient region of Thrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is a hard coal burned as fuel.

clue.text: Austrian poet makes note about the Italian king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
il is the Italian for the
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A poet from Austria writes a memo concerning an Italian monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a Prague-born poet writing in German, an Austrian subject.

clue.text: Part of book on a New Testament spectacle

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a page is one part of a book

explanation.surface: A section of a Bible concerning a grand show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or procession.

clue.text: Return and surrender

definitions.meaning: a return on investment, its profit
to give way or give in

explanation.definitionFit: Yield means the profit an investment brings and also to give in.

clue.text: The cost of monarchic power?

definitions.meaning: a British coin once worth five shillings, so a price
the sovereign's authority, symbolised by the royal headdress

explanation.walkthrough: The crown was a British coin worth five shillings (a quarter of a pound).
explanation.definitionFit: A crown was an old British coin worth five shillings, and also stands for royal authority.

clue.text: "Ay, in the ---- ye go for men" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "Ay, in the ---- ye go for men" (Macbeth)

parts.words: "Ay, in the ---- ye go for men" (Macbeth)
parts.note: fill the gap in Macbeth's line to the murderers, where he says they pass as men only in a list of kinds

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, Act 3 Scene 1: the murderers count as men only in the list of types, as hounds and curs are all called dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a list, the sense Macbeth uses for a mere classification of kinds.

clue.text: End in tin? Surely not this reptile

definitions.text: End in tin? Surely not this reptile

parts.words: End in tin? Surely not this reptile
parts.note: a playful hint: the reptile's name starts with CA and ends in N like a can, yet it is no tinned food

explanation.surface: A creature protests it will never finish up canned.
explanation.definitionFit: A caiman is a Central and South American relative of the alligator.

clue.text: Such a sketch by a liberated worker

parts.note: liberated means set free
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A drawing made by a worker who has been released.
explanation.definitionFit: A freehand drawing is made without ruler or tracing aids.

clue.text: Treatment for many in the process of intervention

indicators.note: in places the small piece inside the longer word

parts.note: mediation is intervening to settle a dispute
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Care given to a crowd while negotiations are under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is C, the Roman hundred, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication is drug treatment given to a patient.

clue.text: One cat among a number in the pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of Asian mountains
there are sixteen of this weight unit in an imperial pound

explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is another name for the snow leopard and a weight, sixteen to the pound.

clue.text: Come across 14 rent in pieces

indicators.note: broken in pieces suggests the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: refers to the answer to 14 across, the snow leopard or weight

explanation.surface: Stumble on a big cat that has been torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them unexpectedly.

clue.text: This country's weather oppresses Scot and Russian

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the last, weighing it down

parts.note: for a British paper this country is the UK
rain is a type of weather
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Britain's climate gets a Scotsman and a Russian down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oppresses' puts UK RAIN above IAN in this down entry; when set, Ukraine was part of the USSR, so a Ukrainian counted as Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine was a Soviet republic when set, so a Ukrainian was loosely called Russian.

clue.text: Study costume and mail elsewhere

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a dress is a costume or garment

explanation.surface: Examine an outfit and post it on to another place.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a letter is to put a new address on it so it is forwarded.

clue.text: Girl in this novel — one skilled in Greek

indicators.note: in tells us the girl's name goes inside the rearranged word
novel means new, so the letters of this are given a new form

parts.note: Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A character in this book turns out to be a classical scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'this book' in the surface but is the anagram signal, making HIST from 'this'; 'in' then houses the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellenist is a scholar of ancient Greek language and culture.

clue.text: Fat makes one ill on an organized manoeuvre

indicators.note: an organized manoeuvre suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Grease makes someone sick during a military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease from sheep's wool, used in ointments.

clue.text: Letter from Greek lawyer for Miss Fleming

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A note from a lawyer in Greece addressed to a woman named Fleming.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhoda Fleming is the heroine of George Meredith's 1865 novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda Fleming is the title character of a Victorian novel by Meredith.

clue.text: Figure cut by Territorial Army commander not quite departed?

indicators.note: being cut by something means it slices into the middle, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding

indicators.note: not quite means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: departed means gone
TA is the abbreviation for Britain's Territorial Army reserve

explanation.surface: An army reserve leader seems almost dead, cutting a poor figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is the definition, a shape; 'cut by' signals the reserve army slicing into the commander plus the almost-departed word; 'not quite' drops the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided plane shape, a geometrical figure.

clue.text: Convenient-sounding headgear for the race

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is said like the synonym

parts.note: handy means convenient
a cap is a piece of headgear

explanation.surface: A hat that seems practical is worn to the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a horse race in which runners carry weights to even their chances.

clue.text: One with possessions may talk foolishly?

definitions.meaning: someone who has things, an owner
to babble or blather, a Scots usage

explanation.definitionFit: A haver is literally one who has, and in Scotland to haver is to babble nonsense.

clue.text: Maybe it's a butterfly that gives 'im a turn

parts.note: a dropped-aitch spelling of him
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: An insect seems to give a man a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the adult stage of an insect, a butterfly for example.

clue.text: Heeled over, as Quixote did

definitions.meaning: leaned to one side like a ship
Don Quixote charged at windmills with his lance

explanation.definitionFit: Tilted means leaned over, and Quixote famously jousted with his lance at windmills.

clue.text: Speed of a bird?

definitions.meaning: a small sandpiper, a wading shorebird

explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a unit of nautical speed and also a species of sandpiper.

clue.text: Rich plebeian native of Sofia changes leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria

explanation.surface: A wealthy commoner from Sofia gets a new head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes leader' swaps the B of BULGARIAN for a V.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse person, typically one newly wealthy and showy.

clue.text: Fireplace in Wardle's home

indicators.note: in asks for the inside of the word, without its first and last letters

parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, Mr Wardle lives at Dingley Dell

explanation.surface: A hearth in a character's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Wardle's farm in The Pickwick Papers is Dingley Dell; the inside of DINGLEY gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Managed an old entertainer in Burma

parts.note: ran means managed, as a business
the Goons were 1950s British radio comedians in The Goon Show

explanation.surface: Someone ran a veteran performer's act in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy starring Spike Milligan and Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital city of Burma.

clue.text: A number of workers in rented accommodation

parts.note: ten is a number
worker ants are the crossword's classic workers

explanation.surface: Several employees are living in a flat they rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants are people who rent and live in property owned by a landlord.
